solution.paragraph: $$L100=1.294,R100=1.301;L100=1.294,R100=1.301;$$ the exact average is between these values.

problem.paragraph: Explain why the graphs of a quadratic function (parabola) $$p(x)$$ and a linear function $$\ell(x)$$ can intersect in at most two points. Suppose that $$p(a) = \ell(a)$$ and $$p(b) = \ell(b),$$ and that $${\int_{a}^{b}{p(t)dt}} > {\int_{a}^{b}{\ell(t)dt}}.$$ Explain why $${\int_{c}^{d}{p(t)}} > {\int_{c}^{d}{\ell(t)dt}}$$ whenever $$a \leq c < d \leq b.$$

Suppose that parabola $$p(x) = ax^{2} + bx + c$$ opens downward $$(a < 0)$$ and has a vertex of $$y = \frac{-b}{2a} > 0.$$ For which interval $$\left\lbrack {A,B} \right\rbrack$$ is $$\int_{A}^{B}{\left( {ax^{2} + bx + c} \right)dx}$$ as large as possible?

solution.paragraph: The integral is maximized when one uses the largest interval on which p is nonnegative. Thus, $$A=-b-b2-4ac2aA=-b-b2-4ac2a$$ and $$B=-b+b2-4ac2a.B=-b+b2-4ac2a.$$

problem.paragraph: Suppose $$\left\lbrack {a,b} \right\rbrack$$ can be subdivided into subintervals $$a = a_{0} < a_{1} < a_{2} < \text{⋯} < a_{N} = b$$ such that either $$f \geq 0$$ over $$\left\lbrack {a_{i - 1},a_{i}} \right\rbrack$$ or $$f \leq 0$$ over $$\left\lbrack {a_{i - 1},a_{i}} \right\rbrack.$$ Set $$A_{i} = {\int_{a_{i - 1}}^{a_{i}}{f(t)dt}}.$$

Suppose f and g are continuous functions such that $${\int_{c}^{d}{f(t)dt}} \leq {\int_{c}^{d}{g(t)dt}}$$ for every subinterval $$\left\lbrack {c,d} \right\rbrack$$ of $$\left\lbrack {a,b} \right\rbrack.$$ Explain why $$f(x) \leq g(x)$$ for all values of x.

solution.paragraph: If $$f(t0)>g(t0)f(t0)>g(t0)$$ for some $$t0\in [a,b],t0\in [a,b],$$ then since $$f-gf-g$$ is continuous, there is an interval containing t0 such that $$f(t)>g(t)f(t)>g(t)$$ over the interval $$[c,d],[c,d],$$ and then $$\int ddf(t)dt>\int cdg(t)dt\int ddf(t)dt>\int cdg(t)dt$$ over this interval.

problem.paragraph: Suppose the average value of f over $$\left\lbrack {a,b} \right\rbrack$$ is 1 and the average value of f over $$\left\lbrack {b,c} \right\rbrack$$ is 1 where $$a < c < b.$$ Show that the average value of f over $$\left\lbrack {a,c} \right\rbrack$$ is also 1.

Suppose that $$\left\lbrack {a,b} \right\rbrack$$ can be partitioned. taking $$a = a_{0} < a_{1} < \text{⋯} < a_{N} = b$$ such that the average value of f over each subinterval $$\left\lbrack {a_{i - 1},a_{i}} \right\rbrack = 1$$ is equal to 1 for each $$i = 1 \text{,…,} N.$$ Explain why the average value of f over $$\left\lbrack {a,b} \right\rbrack$$ is also equal to 1.

solution.paragraph: The integral of f over an interval is the same as the integral of the average of f over that interval. Thus, $$\int abf(t)dt=\int a0a1f(t)dt+\int a1a2f(t)dt+⋯+\int aN+1aNf(t)dt=\int a0a11dt+\int a1a21dt+⋯+\int aN+1aN1dt=(a1-a0)+(a2-a1)+⋯+(aN-aN-1)=aN-a0=b-a.\int abf(t)dt=\int a0a1f(t)dt+\int a1a2f(t)dt+⋯+\int aN+1aNf(t)dt=\int a0a11dt+\int a1a21dt+⋯+\int aN+1aN1dt=(a1-a0)+(a2-a1)+⋯+(aN-aN-1)=aN-a0=b-a.$$ Dividing through by $$b-ab-a$$ gives the desired identity.

problem.paragraph: Suppose that for each i such that $$1 \leq i \leq N$$ one has $${\int_{i - 1}^{i}{f(t)dt}} = i.$$ Show that $${\int_{0}^{N}{f(t)dt}} = \frac{N\left( {N + 1} \right)}{2}.$$
Suppose that for each i such that $$1 \leq i \leq N$$ one has $${\int_{i - 1}^{i}{f(t)dt}} = i^{2}.$$ Show that $${\int_{0}^{N}{f(t)dt}} = \frac{N\left( {N + 1} \right)\left( {2N + 1} \right)}{6}.$$

solution.paragraph: $$\int 0 N f ( t ) d t = \sum i = 1 N \int i - 1 i f ( t ) d t = \sum i = 1 N i 2 = N ( N + 1 ) ( 2 N + 1 ) 6 \int 0 N f ( t ) d t = \sum i = 1 N \int i - 1 i f ( t ) d t = \sum i = 1 N i 2 = N ( N + 1 ) ( 2 N + 1 ) 6$$

problem.paragraph: [T] Compute the left and right Riemann sums L10 and R10 and their average $$\frac{L_{10} + R_{10}}{2}$$ for $$f(t) = t^{2}$$ over $$\left\lbrack {0,1} \right\rbrack.$$ Given that $${\int_{0}^{1}{t^{2}dt}} = 0.\overset{-}{33},$$ to how many decimal places is $$\frac{L_{10} + R_{10}}{2}$$ accurate?

solution.paragraph: $$L10=1.815,R10=1.515,L10+R102=1.665,L10=1.815,R10=1.515,L10+R102=1.665,$$ so the estimate is accurate to two decimal places.

solution.paragraph: a. The graph is antisymmetric with respect to $$t=12t=12$$ over $$[0,1],[0,1],$$ so the average value is zero. b. For any value of a, the graph between $$[a,a+1][a,a+1]$$ is a shift of the graph over $$[0,1],[0,1],$$ so the net areas above and below the axis do not change and the average remains zero.

problem.paragraph: If f is 1-periodic $$\left( f\left( {t + 1} \right) = f(t) \right),$$ odd, and integrable over $$\left\lbrack {0,1} \right\rbrack,$$ is it always true that $${\int_{0}^{1}{f(t)dt}} = 0?$$
If f is 1-periodic and $${\int_{0}^{1}{f(t)dt}} = A,$$ is it necessarily true that $${\int_{a}^{1 + a}{f(t)dt}} = A$$ for all A?

solution.paragraph: Yes, the integral over any interval of length 1 is the same.
